segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and for those of you who have been following, this is the very last episode of our 10-part series about giving a presentation in English.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，对于那些一直关注的人来说，这是我们 10 部分系列中关于用英语进行演示的最后一集。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: This is part 10 where we are going to receive questions from the audience.
segments.zh: 这是第 10 部分，我们将收到观众的问题。

segments.en: So this is called a Q&A session or question and answer session.
segments.zh: 所以这叫做 Q&A session（question and answer session），也就是问答环节。

segments.en: Let's take a listen to our dialogue.
segments.zh: 我们来听听对话。

segments.en: We'll be back in a moment.
segments.zh: 我们马上回来。

segments.en: Well everyone, I'm sure you'd like to join me in thanking Michael for what was a really inspirational presentation.
segments.zh: 好吧，大家，我相信你们都愿意和我一起感谢迈克尔，感谢他带来了一场非常鼓舞人心的演讲。

segments.en: Sincere thanks, Michael.
segments.zh: 真诚的感谢，迈克尔。

segments.en: Now I'm sure many of you will be keen to ask some questions, so I'd like to open up a Q&A session.
segments.zh: 现在我相信你们中很多人都会很想问一些问题，所以我想开启一个问答环节。

segments.en: Please raise your hand if you have any questions at all.
segments.zh: 如果您有任何问题，请举手。

segments.en: Yes, Janice, go ahead.
segments.zh: 是的，珍妮丝，去吧。

segments.en: Yes, thank you, Jonathan.
segments.zh: 是的，谢谢你，乔纳森。

segments.en: I would just like to go back to the comment Mr. Ford made in regards to our competitors, particularly Orange.
segments.zh: 我只想再谈谈福特先生关于我们竞争对手的评论，尤其是 Orange。

segments.en: Now as you know, Orange has established themselves as the market leader in the high-end laptop market.
segments.zh: 如您所知，Orange 已成为高端笔记本电脑市场的市场领导者。

segments.en: How does Mr. Ford expect to compete with a company that has such a huge reputation and huge resources?
segments.zh: 福特先生打算如何与一家声誉极高、资源雄厚的公司竞争？

segments.en: Well Janice, first of all, thanks for a very good question.
segments.zh: 好吧，珍妮丝，首先，感谢一个非常好的问题。

segments.en: I think you have hit the nail on the head actually.
segments.zh: 我觉得你确实说到点子上了。

segments.en: Orange are the global leaders precisely because of their size and power.
segments.zh: 奥兰治之所以成为全球领导者，正是因为他们的规模和力量。

segments.en: But although we can't compete in terms of size, I do believe we hold an advantage in terms of dedication to customer service.
segments.zh: 但是，虽然我们不能在规模方面竞争，但我相信我们在对客户服务的奉献精神方面拥有优势。

segments.en: Yes, I admit this is a David and Goliath battle, but don't forget who won that contest.
segments.zh: 是的，我承认这是大卫对歌利亚、以小搏大的较量，不过别忘了最后是谁赢了。

segments.en: Mr. Ford, could you elaborate on actual technical details of the X420 a little more?
segments.zh: 福特先生，您能否详细说明一下 X420 的实际技术细节？

segments.en: I'd love to, but I think we're a little pressed for time right now.
segments.zh: 我很乐意，不过我想我们现在时间有点紧。

segments.en: However, Jonathan has all the technical specs for you on the PowerPoint presentation, which you can look over in your own time.
segments.zh: 不过，Jonathan 已经在 PowerPoint 演示文稿里为你准备好所有技术规格，你可以有空时看看。

segments.en: Mr. Ford, one final question. Would you like to join me for a game of golf this Sunday?
segments.zh: 福特先生，最后一个问题。 这个星期天你想和我一起打高尔夫球吗？

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So now let's take a look at some words on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以现在让我们来看看一些关于语言要点的单词。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: Well, at the beginning of today's dialogue, Jonathan said, I'm sure many of you will be keen to ask some questions.
segments.zh: 好吧，在今天的对话开始时，乔纳森说，我相信你们中的许多人都会热衷于问一些问题。

segments.en: What does this word keen mean?
segments.zh: keen 这个词是什么意思？

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So to be keen to do something, which basically means that you want to or would like to do something.
segments.zh: 所以要热衷于做某事，这基本上意味着你想或想做某事。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Are you keen?
segments.zh: 你愿意吗？

segments.en: Would you like to do it? Are you interested in doing it?
segments.zh: 你愿意吗? 你有兴趣做吗？

segments.en: Now, this is a very British form of addressing something, right?
segments.zh: 现在，这是一种非常英国的解决问题的形式，对吧？

segments.en: That's right. This is very British.
segments.zh: 没错。 这是非常英国的。

segments.en: We don't really say this as much in America, but you can.
segments.zh: 我们在美国并没有真正这么说，但你可以。

segments.en: People will understand you.
segments.zh: 人们会理解你的。

segments.en: I would say, I'm sure many of you would like to ask some questions and so you could say that both ways.
segments.zh: 我会说，我相信你们中的许多人都想问一些问题，所以你可以两种方式都这么说。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So many people want to ask questions and Jonathan said, so I'd like to open it up to a Q&A session.
segments.zh: 很多人想问问题，乔纳森说，所以我想开启一个问答环节。

segments.en: So the series of words here, to open it up to a Q&A session. What does that mean?
segments.zh: 所以这里的词组是 to open it up to a Q&A session。那是什么意思呢？

segments.en: To open it up.
segments.zh: 开启；开放。

segments.en: It means the discussion. So he would like to invite people to ask questions.
segments.zh: 这意味着讨论。 所以他想邀请人们提问。

segments.en: So I'd like to open it up for questions mean I would like to give you guys the opportunity to ask.
segments.zh: 所以我想打开它来回答问题，这意味着我想给你们一个提问的机会。

segments.en: So to open up a discussion or to open up a conversation, right?
segments.zh: 所以要开启讨论或开启对话，对吧？

segments.en: I would like to open this up to you guys.
segments.zh: 我想把这个机会开放给你们。

segments.en: Okay. Now, one of the audience members asked about another company, which is their competitors and said that they have a huge reputation and huge resources, this competitor.
segments.zh: 好的。 现在，一位观众询问了另一家公司，即他们的竞争对手，并表示他们拥有巨大的声誉和巨大的资源，这个竞争对手。

segments.en: So what is this word reputation?
segments.zh: 那么 reputation 这个词是什么意思呢？

segments.en: Reputation is important.
segments.zh: 声誉很重要。

segments.en: A person can have a reputation, but a company can also have a reputation.
segments.zh: 一个人可以有声誉，但公司也可以有声誉。

segments.en: Now, reputation means the way that other people talk about you.
segments.zh: 现在，声誉意味着其他人谈论你的方式。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So he has a good reputation means people say good things about him.
segments.zh: 所以他有良好的声誉意味着人们对他说好话。

segments.en: Or the media like newspapers and websites, they say good things about him.
segments.zh: 或者像报纸和网站这样的媒体，他们说他的好话。

segments.en: But if you have a bad reputation, it means people are saying bad things about you.
segments.zh: 但如果你的名声不好，这意味着人们在说你的坏话。

segments.en: Right. Okay.
segments.zh: 对。 好的。

segments.en: So that pretty much sums it up a reputation, what other people say about you or how other people see you.
segments.zh: 所以这基本上就概括了 reputation——别人怎么评价你，或者别人怎么看你。

segments.en: So maybe if a company like this has a huge reputation, it means that it's very well respected and people talk very good thing and people talk well about this company.
segments.zh: 所以如果一家这样的公司声誉很高，就意味着它非常受人尊敬，人们对这家公司的评价很好。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Now, another question came along and they wanted to know a little bit more about the technical details of this product that they are introducing.
segments.zh: 现在，另一个问题出现了，他们想更多地了解他们正在介绍的该产品的技术细节。

segments.en: And Mr. Ford said that, you know what, right now we don't really have time, but I'm going to leave all the technical specs on this PowerPoint presentation and you can look at it later.
segments.zh: 福特先生说，你知道吗，现在我们真的没时间，不过我会把所有技术规格留在这个 PowerPoint 演示文稿里，你可以稍后自己看。

segments.en: Okay. So specs, this is something you'll hear very, very often, especially in technical areas, but it means specifications or details.
segments.zh: 好的。 所以规格，这是你会经常听到的，尤其是在技术领域，但它意味着规格或细节。

segments.en: So maybe I have a computer and I know it's an IBM computer, but I don't know the specs.
segments.zh: 所以也许我有一台电脑，我知道它是一台 IBM 计算机，但我不知道规格。

segments.en: I don't have the details.
segments.zh: 我没有细节。

segments.en: So that's something that you would want to find out if you have a problem or you want to look into it more closely. And so specs.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您有问题或想更仔细地研究它，您会想要了解这一点。 所以规格。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay. So these are the specs.
segments.zh: 好的。 所以这些是规格。

segments.en: Now, why don't we take a break?
segments.zh: 现在，我们为什么不休息一下？

segments.en: Let's take a look at our dialogue again and we'll be back in a bit.
segments.zh: 让我们再看看我们的对话，我们会回来的。

segments.en: The first phrase we have here is one that I really like and I use very often. It's, I think you have hit the nail on the head.
segments.zh: 我们这里的第一个短语是我非常喜欢、也经常用的，就是 I think you have hit the nail on the head。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: To hit the nail on the head.
segments.zh: 一针见血；说到点子上。

segments.en: So this is a very common phrase, which basically means I think you got it exactly right.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个非常常见的短语，这基本上意味着我认为你做对了。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So think about a nail that you're hammering something, you have a hammer in your hand.
segments.zh: 所以想想你正在锤击某物的钉子，你的手中有一把锤子。

segments.en: It's very easy to miss, but boom, when you hit it, hit the nail on the head, it means you have it exactly right.
segments.zh: 很容易打偏，但砰的一下，当你正好击中钉子头，也就是 hit the nail on the head，就意味着你完全说对了。

segments.en: That's right.

segments.en: So this was actually a response to one of the questions because it was a very good question and it had a valid point.

segments.en: This is exactly right.

segments.en: So now this is obviously, he's speaking metaphorically, right?

segments.en: That's right.

segments.en: So David and Goliath, that's actually a story that we often talk about.
segments.zh: 所以大卫和歌利亚，这实际上是我们经常谈论的故事。

segments.en: It's a biblical story, so it comes from Christianity and David and Goliath fought, but David was very, very small and Goliath was a monster.

segments.en: He was very big. And so everyone said Goliath will win the fight, but David won the fight.
segments.zh: 他非常大。 所以每个人都说歌利亚会赢得这场战斗，但大卫赢得了这场战斗。

segments.en: And so this is an example or a story that people often use when they say, listen, it may be the case that you think the big giants will win, but actually the small man or our small company will win.
segments.zh: 所以这是人们常说的一类例子或故事：听着，你可能觉得大巨头会赢，但实际上小个子——或者我们这家小公司——会赢。

segments.en: That's right. As you said, we many times make reference to this, even not in the biblical sense, but it's just the size. Maybe we're a small company, we're going to fight this big company. So we say it's a David and Goliath battle or even athletes, maybe two boxers.

segments.en: One is bigger than the other. So they'll say it's a David and Goliath boxing match.
segments.zh: 一个比另一个大。所以他们会说这是一场大卫与歌利亚式的拳击比赛。

segments.en: That's right.

segments.en: That's right.

segments.zh: 我觉得你确实说到点子上了。

segments.en: Orange are the global leaders precisely because of their size and power.
segments.zh: 奥兰治之所以成为全球领导者，正是因为他们的规模和力量。

segments.en: But although we can't compete in terms of size, I do believe we hold an advantage in terms of dedication to customer service.
segments.zh: 但是，虽然我们不能在规模方面竞争，但我相信我们在对客户服务的奉献精神方面拥有优势。

segments.en: Yes, I admit this is a David and Goliath battle, but don't forget who won that contest.
segments.zh: 是的，我承认这是大卫对歌利亚、以小搏大的较量，不过别忘了最后是谁赢了。

segments.en: Mr. Ford, could you elaborate on actual technical details of the X420 a little more?
segments.zh: 福特先生，您能否详细说明一下 X420 的实际技术细节？

segments.en: I'd love to, but I think we're a little pressed for time right now.
segments.zh: 我很乐意，不过我想我们现在时间有点紧。

segments.en: However, Jonathan has all the technical specs for you on the PowerPoint presentation which you can look over in your own time.
segments.zh: 不过，Jonathan 已经在 PowerPoint 演示文稿里为你准备好所有技术规格，你可以有空时看看。

segments.en: Mr. Ford, one final question.
segments.zh: 福特先生，最后一个问题。

segments.en: Would you like to join me for a game of golf this Sunday?
segments.zh: 这个星期天你想和我一起打高尔夫球吗？

segments.en: Alright so that was part 10 of our 10-part series about presentations.
segments.zh: 好吧，这是我们关于演示的 10 部分系列的第 10 部分。

segments.en: We took a look at many different aspects where you can take it as an example as we talked about computers and marketing, but you can more or less have an idea of how a presentation should go and the type of vocab you can use.
segments.zh: 我们看了很多不同的方面，你可以在我们谈论计算机和营销时以它为例，但你或多或少可以了解演示文稿应该如何进行以及您可以使用的词汇类型。

segments.en: That's right, and I think that this particular dialogue today was very, very useful because a lot of times you're going to have people asking you questions and filling in details, and so you can use some of these phrases to help explain exactly what your presentation was about when people do have questions.
segments.zh: 没错，我觉得今天这段对话非常非常有用，因为很多时候人们会向你提问、追问细节，所以当有人提问时，你可以用其中一些短语来帮助准确解释你的演示内容。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So we hope that you enjoyed this series and we would like to hear from you if you have any other suggestions about a series of dialogues or a series of lessons that we can do. We had one about a job interview, all the steps and everything, how a job interview would go. We just had a series about presentations, so maybe you can give us some feedback or some ideas of what you would like to learn. Let us know.
segments.zh: 因此，我们希望您喜欢这个系列，如果您对我们可以做的对话系列或课程系列有任何其他建议，我们希望收到您的来信。我们做过一个关于求职面试的系列，包括所有步骤和整个流程是怎么进行的。我们刚刚做完一个关于演示的系列，所以也许你可以给我们一些反馈，或者告诉我们你想学什么。请告诉我们。

segments.en: Our website is EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 我们的网站是 EnglishPod.com。

segments.en: We'll see you there.
segments.zh: 到时候见。

segments.en: Alright, bye.
segments.zh: 好吧，再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
